bridges.text: The CAR source supplies the pure-state compression and decreasing flags used to distinguish the selected irreducible models. The normalized trace controls the same flags in the later tracial argument.
bridges.title: CAR source, pure states and decreasing flags

bridges.text: Matched shells and their strong operator sums define the concrete generators. The construction keeps one fixed generated C*-algebra rather than replacing it by another algebra with similar relations.
bridges.title: Shell matching and the generated algebra

bridges.text: The capture argument compares nonzero irreducible representations of the generated algebra with its fixed irreducible model. The resulting endpoint gives the single equivalence class and the ordinary counterexample properties.
bridges.title: Capture and classification of irreducible representations

bridges.text: Extend the CAR trace to a state of the same algebra. The CAR-cyclic subspace reduces the target generators and equals the full cyclic GNS space. The extension is then identified uniquely, and the tracial and faithful properties are obtained on this same model.
bridges.title: State extension and the tracial GNS space

bridges.text: The trace GNS construction gives a faithful representation on a separable Hilbert space. This representation is reducible; the exclusion theorem applies to every nonzero irreducible representation on a separable Hilbert space, not merely to the representation selected here.
bridges.title: Faithful separable representation without separable irreducibles

bridges.text: Faithful separable representability bounds the cardinality of the fixed algebra by the continuum. The general lower bound for dense subsets of ordinary Naimark counterexamples yields equality of its cardinality and norm density with the continuum. Combining the example with the general obstruction gives the CH biconditional for density aleph one.
bridges.title: Density, cardinality and CH

overview.hypotheses: The principal construction concerns complex C*-algebras and nonzero irreducible representations. Its fixed algebra and separable faithful tracial representation require no CH hypothesis. CH enters only in the statement equating the continuum with aleph one and the corresponding density-character existence result. The general reverse density obstruction also allows nonunital algebras.
overview.principal_result: A single unital, simple, infinite-dimensional C*-algebra has one unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible representations and a faithful tracial representation on a separable Hilbert space. The normalized trace of its CAR subalgebra extends uniquely among all states of the same generated algebra.
overview.scope_limits: 16 canonical Declaration Cards are linked in this Companion. Source qualification, source-exposition correspondence and human mathematical review are separate records; no line-by-line independent human proof audit is claimed. The CH biconditional is not a forcing or metatheoretic independence certificate. Corollary 6.2 of Brief Draft R1 is mapped to exact formal endpoints together with a standard Hilbert-space consequence. The orthonormal-basis cardinality statement is the standard consequence, not a direct Lean endpoint supplied in this release; it is not a Hamel-dimension statement.
overview.why_it_matters: The construction distinguishes faithful representability on a separable Hilbert space from irreducible representability on such a space. Its cardinality and norm-density consequences connect the fixed example to a general obstruction for Naimark counterexamples.
